title: Phase 2: Repository layer (4 repos + base + tests)
description: Build the async repository layer on top of the Phase 1 FusekiClient. Deliverables: src/graph/repositories/base_repository.py (shared SPARQL helpers, prefix constants, literal escaping, binding helpers), intent_repository.py (create/get/list/update/delete + write_state_change), intent_report_repository.py, intent_spec_repository.py, hub_repository.py, tests/unit/test_repositories.py. SPARQL rules: INSERT DATA for create, SELECT+OPTIONAL for get, COUNT(*) + LIMIT/OFFSET for list, DELETE/INSERT WHERE for update, DROP GRAPH for delete. No RDFLib in production code. Mocked with respx.
close_reason: 59/59 tests passing, 98% coverage. All 5 repository files delivered: base_repository (helpers), intent_repository (create/get/list/update/delete/write_state_change), intent_report_repository, intent_spec_repository, hub_repository. SPARQL rules followed: INSERT DATA for create, SELECT+OPTIONAL for get, COUNT(*)+LIMIT/OFFSET for list, DELETE/INSERT WHERE for update, ASK+DROP for delete. expressionValue stored as opaque xsd:string, deserialized back to dict for JsonLdExpression.

title: Phase 1: Fuseki graph layer (namespaces, nodes, store, schema_init)

Deliverables per docs/09-deliverables.md: src/graph/namespaces.py (namespace constants + named graph URIs), src/graph/nodes.py (URI constructor functions), src/graph/store.py (FusekiClient async httpx class + module singleton), src/graph/schema_init.py (async Fuseki init helpers). Tests in tests/unit/test_store.py using respx to mock HTTP — no live Fuseki required. Must reach ≥80% coverage of src/graph/.
close_reason: All 41 Phase 1 tests passing, 100% coverage of src/graph/ (namespaces, nodes, store, schema_init). Fuseki SPARQL-over-HTTP client fully implemented with respx-mocked tests.

title: Translate dlog rules to Apache Jena format + write docs/12
description: The ontology/rules/ directory contains 15 Datalog rule files written for RDFox. These need to be validated, translated to Apache Jena .rules syntax, and written to ontology/jena-rules/. A design doc docs/12 - load_dlog.md is required covering: dlog vs Jena syntax differences, translation decisions, known limitations (FORALL, NAF), file inventory, and how to load in Fuseki via assembler. Deliverables: docs/12 - load_dlog.md, 13 .rules files in ontology/jena-rules/, one master tio_all.rules concatenating all rules.
close_reason: 13 Jena rule files written to ontology/jena-rules/, docs/12 - load_dlog.md created. All 291 tests still passing at 98.38% coverage.

title: Fix test_generated_models.py: 6 LifecycleStatus failures (NameError + missing can_transition_to)
description: TestLifecycleStateMachine uses LifecycleStatus.ACKNOWLEDGED, LifecycleStatus.ACTIVE etc. and calls .can_transition_to() on them. Two problems: (1) LifecycleStatus is not imported (same commented-out import as the fixture bug), and (2) can_transition_to() does not exist on the generated Pydantic model — the FSM lives in src/services/state_machine.py as validate_transition(from, to). Fix: either (a) add a LifecycleStatus enum with can_transition_to() to the patched generated models via scripts/patch_generated_models.py, or (b) rewrite TestLifecycleStateMachine to call state_machine.validate_transition() directly, which is the actual implementation being tested.

title: Fix test_generated_models.py: 25 fixture errors (Intent, IntentPatch not found)
description: tests/unit/test_generated_models.py has its import block commented out. Classes like Intent, IntentPatch, JsonLdExpression, TurtleExpression are used as pytest fixture parameters (e.g. def test_missing_name_raises(self, Intent)) but no fixtures with those names are defined anywhere. pytest fails at setup with 'fixture Intent not found' for all 25 affected tests. Fix: add a conftest.py in tests/unit/ that imports these classes from src.api.schemas.generated and exposes them as fixtures, or uncomment and correct the import in test_generated_models.py and convert the test methods to not use fixture injection for plain class references.
